newsitem.title: UK: No change to LME's ring/inter-office trading split.
newsitem.headline: No change to LME's ring/inter-office trading split.

text.p: The London Metal Exchange is to keep its dual method of trading unchanged, with inter-office business and open-outcry ring trading continuing, LME Chief Executive David King said on Thursday.
The current split between telephone trading and floor business was touched on briefly in the Securities and Investments Board (SIB) review of the LME, which was published today.

"There is no impetus to change. More transparency is achievable within the current system," King said. In its review the SIB noted the lack of post-trade transparency of LME futures and options during inter-office trading periods.
It recommended that the LME publish indicators of price and volume in relation to inter-office trade drawn from its existing systems.
The SIB, Britain's top regulator, was asked by the LME to carry out a top-to-bottom review of the LME after the Sumitomo scandal shocked world metal markets in June.
In mid-June, Sumitomo Corp of Japan fired its head copper trader Yasuo Hamanaka, alleging he admitted running up losses of $2.6 billion in unauthorised copper trading.
